newsitem.title: DUBAI: HORSE RACING-U.S. DUO FANCIED TO FOLLOW CIGAR'S FOOTSTEPS.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-U.S. DUO FANCIED TO FOLLOW CIGAR'S FOOTSTEPS.

text.p: Two American horses foaled in Brazil are favourites for the world's richest horse race, the $4 million Dubai World Cup, to be run next Saturday.

Last year's inaugural running of the event over 2,000 metres (a mile and a quarter) of Dubai's desert sand was won by Cigar, the now-retired American colt, dubbed wonder horse for his 14 wins in a row.
This year's championship for 13 older middle-distance horses from five continents features the two Brazilian-born Americans -- Siphon and Sandpit, both trained in California by Richard Mandella.
The European challenge is headed by Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe winner Helissio of France and English-trained Singspiel, who triumphed in the Japan Cup last November, edging Helissio into third place.

Gambling is banned in the United Arab Emirates but British bookmakers rate the two U.S. professional dirt horses first and second favourites at 3-1 and 7-2 ahead of Helissio, joint third-favourite on 5-1 with Singspiel.
Singspiel is one of two entries from the man who inspired the race, Sheikh Mohammed, Dubai's crown prince and the world's most successful owner-breeder.
Dubai World Cup committee member Brough Scott said: "Bookies in Britain think that the American horses will win again, as they did last year, because sand is their home surface.

"They are the best two horses ever to come from that home of footballers but not normally of good racehorses, Brazil. Brazil has never had a Group One top class horse running in the northern hemisphere before," Scott said.

"They are very impressive. Siphon is a horse who goes into the lead and goes flat out from the start. He's the horse who broke Cigar's winning streak last August in the Pacific Classic in California. He went out very fast and Cigar took him on and basically he broke Cigar and something else came by both of them. And that's what ended Cigar's reign."
Sandpit's only run to date on sand ended in second place behind Siphon in the biggest race of the year so far, the Santa Anita Handicap.
Singspiel, though not rated as good as Helissio, travels well. He ran second in the Breeders' Cup in Toronto last autumn, and then carried off the Japan Cup.

He is a clear danger although top jockey Frankie Dettori has deserted him for the improving Kammtarra, who raced in England last year but has been campaigning with success on the dirt at Dubai's Nad al-Sheba track.
The draw for Saturday's race is on Tuesday at midday (0800 GMT).
British bookmakers Ladbrokes bet: 3-1 Siphon, 7-2 Sandpit, 5-1 Helissio, Singspiel, 6-1 Formal Gold, 10-1 Kammtarra, 20-1 Even Top, Hokuto Vega, Juggler and Key of Luck, 25-1 Luso, 33-1 Bijou d'Inde.
